Zcash · private markets · intents

Intents signed and sealed with post-quantum keys, settled in shielded ZEC.

An intent is signed with ML-DSA-65 and sealed to the solver with ML-KEM-768. The user escrows testnet ZEC, the solver delivers from its own liquidity, and a verifier releases or refunds the escrow. It writes every decision as a signed, hash-chained log entry, anchored in a shielded memo. Zcash spends stay elliptic-curve. The post-quantum part is the intent layer.

Sign

ML-DSA-65 over the canonical intent; the key id is inside it.

Seal

ML-KEM-768 + HKDF + AES-256-GCM to the solver's key.

Settle

Shielded funding, fill and payout, each read with a viewing key.

Sign the decision

The verifier's ML-DSA-65 log, hash-chained and anchored.

What is post-quantum, and what is not

Post-quantum

  • The intent signature (ML-DSA-65)
  • The sealed envelope to the solver (ML-KEM-768): recording it today does not open it later
  • The verifier's signatures on every decision

Not post-quantum

  • Zcash spends and note encryption: a future quantum adversary holding the chain could read the funding and fill memos and link them
  • The escrow viewing key is public, so funding amounts and intent hashes are visible today

Limits

read before trusting it
  • Not trustless. The verifier holds the escrow and could withhold a payout. It cannot change the record without the signatures, links or anchors showing it.
  • The solver and the verifier read the plaintext intent. In this run, one receive address served all three intents, so those deliveries can be linked.
  • Anchors are periodic, and each names the one before it. The escrow's full viewing key is published, so every anchor it sent can be listed and a second head is a visible fork; entries after the last anchor are not covered. Funding and fills need 3 confirmations.
  • ZEC only, testnet only, a single verifier key, not audited. A portfolio piece: the Zecathon entry is Shielded x402.
